topic.subject: science
topic.title: Chemical effects of electric current
topic.scope: conduction in liquids, electrolysis basics, electroplating, tester with LED

misconceptions.statement: All liquids conduct electricity equally well.
misconceptions.why: Students often think of liquids as a single category like solids or gases without considering chemical composition.
misconceptions.fix: Only liquids containing dissolved salts, acids, or bases (electrolytes) conduct electricity; pure water is a poor conductor.

probe.question: Will distilled water light up an LED in a tester?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because all water conducts electricity.

misconceptions.statement: Electricity flows through liquids just like it flows through metal wires.
misconceptions.why: Students visualize current as a flow of electrons in all materials, ignoring the role of ions in liquids.
misconceptions.fix: In liquids, electricity is carried by the movement of charged particles called ions, not by free electrons as in metals.

probe.question: How does current move through a salt solution?
probe.wrong_answer: Electrons jump from one end of the wire to the other through the liquid.

misconceptions.statement: The chemical change in a liquid happens only at the battery, not at the electrodes.
misconceptions.why: Students associate the power source as the sole cause of all changes in a circuit.
misconceptions.fix: Chemical reactions occur specifically at the surfaces of the electrodes where the current enters and leaves the liquid.

probe.question: Where do bubbles form during the electrolysis of water?

misconceptions.statement: Electroplating is just painting a metal with a liquid metal.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the physical appearance of a shiny coating with the process of painting.
misconceptions.fix: Electroplating is a chemical process where metal ions from a solution are deposited onto an object using electric current.

probe.question: How does copper get onto a spoon during electroplating?
probe.wrong_answer: The spoon is dipped in liquid copper paint and dried.

misconceptions.statement: The metal being coated disappears into the solution and is gone forever.
misconceptions.why: Students struggle with the conservation of matter in chemical reactions.
misconceptions.fix: The metal ions in the solution are replenished by the anode, maintaining a balance in the electrolyte.

probe.question: What happens to the copper plate (anode) during copper plating?
probe.wrong_answer: It just sits there and does not change.
